learning.title: Hotfixes may run QA and review in parallel, but the merge still waits for BOTH verdicts at the head
learning.body:
On #516 (2026-11-17) I minted the QA and review rows in parallel to move the lease_token_hash hotfix fast — fine for speed — but then MERGED at 03:28Z on reviewer-approval + green CI while the QA row was still open. qa2's Approve arrived at 03:5xZ and converged the record, but the convergence was luck-adjacent, not process: had qa2's re-probe failed, the inverted order would have shipped a break on a lane that existed precisely because main was already broken.
Rule, pinned for hotfix lanes explicitly: parallel verdicts are allowed (and desirable for hotfix speed), but the merge gate is unchanged — BOTH the QA and the review verdict must bind the merging head BEFORE merge. A hotfix's urgency argues for parallel lanes, never for a shorter gate. The same discipline I held #518 to ("merge held for QA verdict per the loop") applies to every merge, and the hotfix is the lane where the temptation to skip it is strongest.
